chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Why did I see you in the presence of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yaqoub?' He said, 'He is my maternal uncle.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is saying a great saying about Allah; He describes Allah, but He cannot be described. So either you sit with him and leave us, or you sit with us and leave him.' I said, 'He says whatever he wishes. What is upon me from him if I do not say what he says?' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not fear that an affliction might descend with him so it would hit all of you together? Do you not know of the one who was from the companions of Musa (peace be upon him), and his father was from the companions of Pharaoh? So when the cavalry of Pharaoh caught up with Musa (peace be upon him), he remained behind from him in order to advise his father, and he was coercing him until they reached a part of the sea, so they both drowned. The news came to Musa (peace be upon him) and he said: 'He is in the Mercy of Allah, but the affliction, when it descends, there is no defence to it from the one who is close to the sinner.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ مُوسَى: Companions of Musa (peace be upon him)
key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yaqoub, a prominent companion known for his theological views
key_terms.وَلَا يُوصَفُ: But He cannot be described (in a limited sense)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of sitting with the sinners according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) warns his companion against excessive familiarity with the 'people of disobedience,' specifically his ungodly maternal uncle, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, to avoid shared divine retribution. He illustrates this principle using the Quranic narrative of a companion of Musa (peace be upon him) who stayed behind to admonish his father, resulting in both drowning together; while the father was in mercy, the companion suffered the affliction due to his proximity. This highlights the Shia scholarly concept of 'qaraba' (closeness) as a factor in sharing the consequences of sin, even if one's own status is righteous.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Muhammad, from Al Ja’fary who said,

‘Why did I<sup>asws</sup> see you being in the presence of Abdul Rahman Bin Yaqoub?’ So he said, ‘He is my maternal uncle’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is saying such words about Allah<sup>azwj</sup> which are grievous. He describes Allah<sup>azwj</sup> but He<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be described. So either you sit with him and leave us<sup>asws</sup>, or you sit with us<sup>asws</sup> and leave him’. 
So I said, ‘He is saying whatever he so desires to. Which thing is it upon me from him, when I do not say what he is saying?’ So Abu Al-Hassan<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Do you not fear that an affliction might descend with him so it would hit all of you together? Do you not know of the one who was from the companions of Musa<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, and his father was from the companions of the Pharaoh<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup>, so when the cavalry of Pharaoh<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup> caught up with Musa<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, he remained behind from him<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> in order to advise his father, and he was coercing him until a wave from the sea reached him, so all of them drowned.
So the news came to Musa<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘He is in the Mercy of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, but the affliction, when it does descend, there is no defence to it from the one who is close to the sinner’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Bakr ibn Muhammad from al-Ja’fari who has said the following:

“I heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) saying, ‘Why is it that I find you with ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya’qub?’ I (the narrator) then said, ‘It is because he is my uncle from my mother’s side.’ The Imam said, ‘He says great heavy words about Allah. He describes Allah who is beyond description. You either sit with him and leave us or sit with us and leave him.’ I then said, ‘He may say anything he wants but what does that have to do with me when I say none of the things that he says?’ Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) said, ‘Are you not afraid of the misfortune that may befall him and involve all of you also? Do you not know about the thing that happened to the people of Moses? The father of one of them was of the people of the Pharaoh. When the Pharaoh’s horsemen approached Moses, he withdrew himself from Moses to convince his father to join Moses but his father kept moving while he argued against his father until they reached the shore and both were drowned. The news reached Moses and he said, ‘He is in the mercy of Allah, but when misfortune falls there is no defense for those who are close to the sinners.’”
